races.name: Racing TV EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Happy Birthday Katie Exon Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Great
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with solid Good-going form including a recent win at 6f; drops in from 6f-7f trips, which may mean the 5f on fast ground comes just a touch sharply, but Shane Gray has ridden the yard's recent winners and 11 days' freshness is not a concern.

runners_data.name: Dc Cogent
runners_data.note: Consistent at 5f on Good ground with two placed efforts from five tries at this trip; Bryan Smart's yard is out of form (0/5 in 14 days) which is a meaningful flag, and 34 days off adds a small fitness query — does best when pace is strong enough to bring his hold-up style into play.

runners_data.name: Hurt You Never
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has run exclusively on Good or faster ground (15/15) with two wins and four places, so the surface is firmly in his favour; races from behind and needs a true pace to produce his best, but Adrian Nicholls' yard has only one winner from nine recently and Jack Nicholls takes off 5lb which partially compensates.

runners_data.name: Level Up
runners_data.note: Despite being plotted in midfield, this is a confirmed hold-up horse best suited to being produced late — the redistribution reflects a crowded closer's group, not his actual racing pattern; PJ McDonald is a major booking, 0/3W on Good at 5f in recent form but consistently placed, and the tongue strap is already established headgear.

runners_data.name: Dream Deal
runners_data.note: Strong recent 5f form — a win and two seconds on Good ground — makes him one of the classier performers on current going-specific evidence; although a genuine hold-up runner squeezed into the midfield map, David Allan rides him with the confidence of a trainer (Easterby, 9/72 in 14 days) in solid form, and only 5 days since last run needs noting.

runners_data.name: Beerwah
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front runner who should enjoy an uncontested lead throughout; two 5f Good-ground wins in recent form, blinkered, and Jack Callan's 3lb claim is useful — the concern is the STYLE_FIT flag suggesting it may not always get an easy lead, though in this field it almost certainly will.

runners_data.name: Toptime
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a Beverley course win and a recent third at this trip on Good ground; races prominently and is very comfortable on quick surfaces (1W3P at Good/Good-to-Firm), making it a consistent each-way option if the pace unfolds at a fair tempo from Beerwah.

runners_data.name: Bibendum
runners_data.note: Recent 5f winner who races from a prominent position; visor fitted, Julie Camacho's yard returned one winner from 16 in the last 14 days which tempers confidence slightly, and most of his best form has come on softer surfaces — the fast ground here warrants a small query.

runners_data.name: Dandy Dinmont
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up runner whose sole recent win came at this trip on Good ground, but with nine hold-up types in the field he is mapped to midfield and unlikely to find his natural position; Nigel Tinkler in reasonable form (2/18 in 14 days) and 13 days off are neutral factors, but the style compromise is real.

runners_data.name: Opal Storm
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field (OR 55) and a true hold-up type racing wide of its natural position due to field congestion; Faye McManoman is a conditional and the yard has had just one runner in 14 days — the tp headgear and a recent 5f win on Standard offer some encouragement but the class gap and positional squeeze make this a difficult profile.

races.paceDynamic: Beerwah is the sole confirmed front runner and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, should slot cleanly to the front and control a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over Beverley's straight five furlongs. Toptime and Bibendum will push forward from the prominent group to fill the early positions just behind, creating a compact lead bunch but not the sort of contested pace that would burn Beerwah off. The field carries a significant number of hold-up types — Level Up, Dream Deal, Dandy Dinmont and Opal Storm are all genuine closers who have been mapped to midfield precisely because there is no room for all of them at the rear; of these, Dream Deal and Level Up are most likely to actually secure their preferred back-of-the-field position given their proven ability to switch off. With Beerwah dictating an uncontested, measured pace on quick ground, this shape strongly favours hold-up horses that can finish with purpose over the final two furlongs, provided the pace is genuinely honest — but with only one pace-setter, the tempo may be just steady enough to flatter the prominent racers who can track and kick from just off the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Beerwah Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Beerwah secures the lead uncontested and Toptime/Bibendum track without forcing a genuine pace duel.
scenarios.body: Beerwah dictates a controlled tempo, conserving enough to sprint for home entering the final furlong on the fast surface; horses tracking closely off the pace are ideally placed to pounce but the leader's freshness after 25 days and its Good going form (2W on similar) gives it a serious each-way platform.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace Beerwah sets is genuinely honest and the true closers find daylight in the straight to finish hard.
scenarios.body: A decent tempo from Beerwah stretches the field enough that Dream Deal or Level Up, tracking from midfield-rear, can power through on the fast ground to catch the leader in the final 100 yards; Dream Deal's recent 1-2-2-1 form at 5f on Good and Level Up's consistency at short odds make them the prime candidates.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Beerwah's early advantage is eroded by Toptime or Bibendum pressing forward and a genuine mini-duel develops.
scenarios.body: A contested pace would compromise Beerwah and open the race to whichever prominent runner settles best, with Toptime's course-and-distance experience on Good ground (1W at Beverley) making it the likelier beneficiary; Bibendum, fresh off a win at this trip, would also be in the mix through the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Caught In Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is falsely slow and the redistributed hold-up horses cannot find a clear passage up the straight.
scenarios.body: With the bulk of the field bunching mid-race, horses like Dandy Dinmont and Opal Storm — both genuine hold-up types operating out of their natural position — get squeezed for room and cannot deliver their late run; the race effectively becomes a sprint between those who track the leader, with the winner likely already on the premises entering the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Beerwah secures the lead unchallenged — watch whether Jack Callan allows the horse to roll along or deliberately settles, as the tempo he sets in the opening furlong will define the entire race shape.

Dream Deal is only 5 days since its last run; watch the paddock closely for any signs of residual fatigue, as a tired horse sent forward from hold-up position could both compromise its own chance and disrupt the closers behind it.

Level Up, Dandy Dinmont and Opal Storm are all genuine closers but mapped to midfield — watch for early scrimmaging as these runners attempt to drop away from the pace, which could cause interference through the first two furlongs.

Toptime has Beverley course form and races prominently — if it tracks Beerwah smoothly and is travelling well at the two-furlong marker, it becomes the most dangerous rival to the leader in a pace-controlled scenario.

Great drops back from 6f-7f trips to 5f here — watch whether Shane Gray rides it closer than usual to compensate for the shorter trip, as a positional change could alter how effective its finishing kick proves on fast ground.

races.name: Skybet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: It Just Takes Time
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer aged 8 with strong recent placed form at 7f on Good ground (2nd twice in last two runs), handles this trip well, and Jack Garritty's local knowledge is an asset; Mark Walford's stable at 2/19 in 14 days is not setting the world alight but this horse's profile slots neatly into the likely race shape.

runners_data.name: Glenfinnan
runners_data.note: Callum Rodriguez partners a genuine hold-up horse whose single course win came over 8f — this trip is a quarter-furlong short of the optimum, but Good to Firm poses no concern; headgear-free and 16 days fresh, the horse needs the front rank to fold late and is the most credible closer in the field if the scenario allows.

runners_data.name: A War Eagle
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone pace-setter on Good to Firm, 45 days since last run but with a course win and two wins from 13 starts in similar going; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) applies here less as a concern and more as a reminder that its lead will be uncontested — the question is whether it stays on over this distance rather than whether it secures the front.

runners_data.name: Tattie Bogle
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with two wins at 7-8f and a strong placed record, but a natural front-runner whose instinct to race prominently is frustrated in this field by A War Eagle's confirmed lead role; Charlie Johnston's yard is in excellent 14-day form (7/65) and Rowan Scott rides, though the positional compromise is real — the horse's best form comes when allowed to stride on rather than race in the pack.

runners_data.name: Coolree
runners_data.note: Has won twice recently, both from the front over 8f, and arrives here fitted with a tongue-tie (tp) while reverting to 7½f; Sam England's smaller yard (2/11 in 14 days) has modest strike-rate context, and like Tattie Bogle this horse's front-running instincts are squeezed out by A War Eagle — Jack Nicholls (5lb claimer) adds a small weight advantage but the style displacement is the key factor to weigh.

races.paceDynamic: A War Eagle is the confirmed lone front-runner here and, with only four rivals in a five-horse field, faces zero genuine challenge for the lead on Good to Firm ground over 7½f at Beverley. The pace will be sustainable rather than pressured, giving A War Eagle a chance to control fractions and ensure the race is run to suit a prominent-to-lead profile throughout. Tattie Bogle and Coolree are both natural prominent types who want to race forward but cannot both occupy that position alongside A War Eagle — one or both will be shuffled back into a midfield role that does not suit their best form. It Just Takes Time and Glenfinnan are the only runners genuinely equipped to come from off the pace, meaning this race shape structurally favours the hold-up and late-finishing profile if the solo front-runner's lead becomes generous, but the most likely outcome is that an unchallenged A War Eagle controls the race and prominent types who track closely benefit most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If A War Eagle secures the lead unchallenged and controls a measured gallop on Good to Firm ground.
scenarios.body: A War Eagle dictates every inch of the pace, never forced to quicken sharply, and simply sustains its advantage to the line on a surface it handles; the prominent horses who manage to track closely — particularly It Just Takes Time — are ideally placed to mount the nearest challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaser Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If A War Eagle's early control is tracked tightly by Tattie Bogle, who secures a closer position than the pace map suggests.
scenarios.body: Tattie Bogle, a natural front-runner with strong course-distance form and two wins at this trip, overcomes positional compromise to sit just off the leader and produces a finishing effort that picks off a tiring A War Eagle inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is generous enough and the front rank ties itself up, allowing Glenfinnan to deliver a sustained run from the rear.
scenarios.body: Glenfinnan, whose best win came over 8f and who is comfortable in similar ground, finds the gaps down the straight and finishes strongly past a field that has spent itself in the lead duel; Good to Firm suits and Callum Rodriguez gives the horse a confident hold-up ride.

watchPoints.text: A War Eagle's 45-day absence is worth monitoring in-running — if it hits a flat spot in the final two furlongs having led throughout, It Just Takes Time or Glenfinnan are positioned to capitalise.

Tattie Bogle and Coolree will contest the position just behind A War Eagle early on — watch for either pushing forward and pressuring the leader, which would fundamentally change the race shape from a controlled solo lead to a contested pace.
Glenfinnan's stamina for 7½f is unproven at this trip on its recent form (most runs over 8f) — if the pace is too steady it may lack the turn of foot to peg back the leader from off the pace.

Good to Firm is confirmed by the going report for this race — all five runners carry an OK going flag, but A War Eagle's two wins on similar ground make it statistically the most comfortable performer on today's surface.

Charlie Johnston's yard is in strong 14-day form (7/65) and Tattie Bogle represents the most live statistical threat from the barn angle — worth tracking if it can secure a forward position despite the pace dynamics working against it.

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Hull Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ice Show
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for O'Meara and Rowan Scott stepping up sharply from 5-6f to 7½f, with zero wins or places on similar going and a form string of 5560 — the trip looks a significant stretch and she is unlikely to be competitive here.

runners_data.name: Bantz
runners_data.note: Form figures of 0-0797 tell a bleak story, and though his natural inclination is to race further back than midfield, today's crowded hold-up division means he is unlikely to get the clean passage he needs; Alan Brown's yard has placed 0 from 11 in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Ryefield
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish, with all recent runs over 5-6f and now asked to stay 7½f — a stamina query hangs over him, and his Mullaney yard has had a quiet spell; the step up in trip looks the primary concern.

runners_data.name: King Sharja
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's consistent six-year-old has placed twice at this course and trip on good ground and carries top weight of 138lbs; a natural hold-up horse whose record of 1W2P on similar going makes him one of the more reliable each-way claims if he finds a position close enough to the pace.

runners_data.name: African Spirit
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' five-year-old has shown flashes at 7-8f on good ground but his hold-up style is genuinely compromised today — a field this light on pace means he must travel wider or later than ideal; tongue strap fitted, and STYLE_FIT 0.91 reflects the positional challenge.

runners_data.name: Back From Dubai
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the race for Bowring and George Wood, last seen winning over 7f on soft ground 36 days ago; good-to-firm at Beverley suits front-runners who get a lead, and unchallenged control of the pace is his primary weapon — the entire race map pivots around him.

runners_data.name: Walk On Walk On
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Noel Wilson with two places at 8f on good ground; shown here in midfield because the hold-up group is oversized, but he has raced prominently at times and a second in similar conditions 16 days ago keeps him in the frame if he can get closer to the pace than his redistribution suggests.

runners_data.name: Itszaboy
runners_data.note: Tinkler's three-year-old has a consistent line of finishes around 6th-7th on good ground with no wins or places in six recent runs; mapped to midfield from a true hold-up berth, and Faye McManoman takes 3lb — that allowance may not be enough to overcome a modest recent profile.

runners_data.name: Alice's Influence
runners_data.note: P J McDonald is a significant jockey booking for David Evans' three-year-old, who has placed in five of her last six at 8f on good or good-to-soft ground; her hold-up style is naturally suited to getting a late run but she too is redistributed from the rear — if McDonald can manoeuvre her into a clear lane, her consistent form figures make her the most interesting of the displaced closers.

races.paceDynamic: Back From Dubai is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner handicap over 7½f on good-to-firm ground at Beverley, and with no genuine rival to press him early, he is likely to control the tempo from the outset at a measured, sustainable gallop. The remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up types — African Spirit, Walk On Walk On, Itszaboy, Bantz, and Alice's Influence are all natural closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the race simply cannot accommodate that many horses at the rear; in reality, several will be jostling for similar ground through the middle stages rather than enjoying clean air at the back. King Sharja and Ice Show add further hold-up weight to the field, meaning the pursuit of Back From Dubai will be congested and potentially untidy as the field strings out around Beverley's turning track. This race shape — a lone leader setting a controlled pace with a wall of hold-up horses unable to all find clean passages — strongly favours the front-runner Back From Dubai and any horse capable of tracking him from a prominent position, with deep closers facing a tactical puzzle rather than a straight sprint finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Back From Dubai Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Back From Dubai meets no serious early challenge and dictates a steady-to-moderate gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: He bowls along unchallenged on the front end, setting his own rhythm on going that suits fast-ground front-runners, and the congested hold-up brigade behind him struggles to co-ordinate a meaningful challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse manages to sit just off Back From Dubai's early pace and picks him off in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With the pace controlled rather than searching, a horse close enough to the leader through the bend gets first run and Back From Dubai ties up after his uncontested lead; Beverley's straight rewards horses who travel well into the straight with cover.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If Back From Dubai sets a pace that proves just quick enough to string the field, opening lanes for a finisher.
scenarios.body: One of the redistributed closers — most likely Alice's Influence or African Spirit, both with decent recent form at this trip and going — finds a gap late and picks off tiring rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Fades, Melee
scenarios.trigger: If Back From Dubai goes too fast too soon or the field bunches and multiple hold-up runners cause interference in the straight.
scenarios.body: A scrappy finish results from traffic issues among the closers; any horse who managed to get a prominent but uncontested berth early benefits most from the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Back From Dubai's early sections — if he gets a clean break and no horse goes with him, he could control this race wire to wire; watch whether any jockey elects to shadow him from the gun.
Alice's Influence and King Sharja will both be angling for similar ground through the bend; if they meet traffic or block each other, the hold-up scenario collapses for both.
Ryefield's stamina — he has never raced beyond 6f and the fading-in-finish flag combined with a 7½f trip on a turning track could see him drop out quickly in the final two furlongs.

Beverley's straight is relatively short after the turn, which compresses the time available for hold-up horses to make their move — watch for jockeys asking for effort earlier than expected rounding the bend.

races.name: Sky Bet For The Fans Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Elettaria
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up specialist whose recent form string of 558734 shows consistency without a win in 15 similar-going starts; John Wainwright sends her back 21 days later but her deepest-closing style is genuinely compromised in a small field at a restrained tempo — she is a true rear-runner squeezed into a midfield slot on the map.

runners_data.name: Inspiring Speeches
runners_data.note: Sara Ender's five-year-old is the lone front-runner here and holds a trainer who is 2/4 in the last 14 days; the 8/15 similar-going record includes a win, and over 1m2f–1m6f on Good this horse has the stamina base to dictate — the style-fit flag simply notes that in a field with more pace it might not get its own way so easily, but that concern evaporates today.

runners_data.name: Copper And Five
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's ten-year-old was placed twice on similar going at 8f and is fresh off a 4-day turnaround; the 1/2P record on comparable ground suggests it finds a level late but the key appeal is its ability to sit close to the pace — at a distance and going it handles, this horse is structurally well placed.

runners_data.name: Defence Missile
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt has gone 0/17 in the last fortnight and this four-year-old's best form comes at 6–8f on Good, shorter than today's 1m½f; a natural hold-up type whose recent runs at 7–8f on Good went 5th, 9th, 8th — it is bumped into a midfield slot on the map but is genuinely not wired to get the run of this race.

runners_data.name: Mavetheforcebewivu
runners_data.note: Alan Brown's four-year-old holds a recent second at 8f on Good and wears a visor, which can sharpen early focus; however it is a natural come-from-behind type nudged toward midfield on the map, and 0W1P in 15 similar-going starts underlines that it finds a way into the frame occasionally without landing the blow — trip stretching to 1m½f is an additional question mark.

runners_data.name: Ring Of Gold
runners_data.note: Michael and David Easterby send out this nine-year-old returning after 30 days with a visor; sim-going record of 0W0P from 15 runs at comparable conditions is brutally honest, and while the 4/31 trainer strike rate in the last fortnight shows some stable activity, this horse's hold-up style in a slowly-run race over a trip it has not won at is a stacking of negatives.

runners_data.name: Royal Sizzler
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the ride on Michael Dods's lightly-raced three-year-old carrying a 8lb pull in the weights at 127lbs; only four career starts and 0W0P on similar going, but at 10f on Good the horse finished fourth — the step back to 1m½f from a 10f base could see it travel kindly if it settles, and Fallon's ability to find a position makes this one to monitor from midfield.

races.paceDynamic: Inspiring Speeches is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 1m½f Beverley classified stakes and, with no genuine rival willing to chase them into the first turn, they should control proceedings at a measured, uncontested tempo on ground riding Good To Firm throughout the card. That sustainable gallop set by a single pace-maker over a flat mile and a half on quick ground is a classic setup for a prominent or tracking horse to sit just off the leader, conserve energy through the middle mile, and outgun the field in the straight. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Defence Missile, Mavetheforcebewivu, Ring Of Gold, and Elettaria all have natural come-from-behind profiles but are redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning they are unlikely to find the ground or gaps they truly need in a race run at a controlled pace. The tactical verdict is clear: horses capable of racing prominently or tracking the leader through the middle stages hold the structural advantage here, with deep closers facing a race run too economically for them to reel in those who have travelled sweetly in the slipstream.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Inspiring Speeches Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Inspiring Speeches bowls along unchallenged and sets a measured pace that plays to the strengths of a prominent tracker.
scenarios.body: Inspiring Speeches dictates from the front at a fair but manageable gallop, and any horse able to sit a length or two off them through the middle stages is perfectly placed for the straight; no other runner has the will to push them along and test their stamina. Copper And Five, with a habit of placing prominently and consistent form at this trip and going, is ideally suited to latching onto this rhythm.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Picks Up Scraps
scenarios.trigger: If Inspiring Speeches sets a pace fractionally quicker than expected and ties up slightly in the closing stages, giving a midfield tracker a run.
scenarios.body: A touch more pace than the leader intends means those racing in mid-division get a rhythm to aim at and find the winner stopping in front of them late; Copper And Five or Royal Sizzler, both comfortable at this trip, could pounce. This remains a secondary shape because the redistributed hold-up horses are not natural closers in this context and the pace is unlikely to be genuinely searching.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and a genuine closer threads through to nail a tiring field.
scenarios.body: One of the redistributed hold-up types — most plausibly Mavetheforcebewivu given a recent second on similar going, or Defence Missile — finds a clear run from midfield as the early leader fades inside the final furlong. This is structurally discounted because none of the true closers are likely to secure their natural wide or late position in a small field run at a controlled tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Bunches Field
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners surge to challenge Inspiring Speeches early, creating a truly-run race that turns into a stamina test.
scenarios.body: An uncharacteristically fierce early battle leaves the front section exhausted and bunches the field, theoretically opening the race to hold-up horses racing their true style late; Ring Of Gold or Elettaria could theoretically benefit at long odds. Given only one confirmed front-runner and a field of predominantly passive riders, this scenario is the least likely outcome on the day.

watchPoints.text: Inspiring Speeches — if Tom Kiely-Marshall (5) gets them into a comfortable rhythm unchallenged inside the opening half-mile, they could control the race so thoroughly that no hold-up horse has a realistic target to run at in the straight.

Copper And Five — a 4-day turnaround after 8 runs at 8f raises the question of whether Ruth Carr deliberately shortens the recovery cycle ahead of a bold front-tracking effort at 12f, which would signal clear stable confidence.

Royal Sizzler — the 8lb weight advantage over rivals is a genuine structural edge in a classified stakes, and Cieren Fallon rarely wastes it; watch where the three-year-old settles in the first two furlongs as a guide to whether it will be competitive late.

Mavetheforcebewivu — the visor reapplication and 6-day turnaround suggest connections want this horse sharp and on its toes, but the gap between natural running style and where the race map places it means punters should watch whether Barry McHugh actively hunts a position or drops back naturally.

Ring Of Gold — 30 days off and 0W0P in 15 runs on comparable going is a red flag for in-running support; if it drifts noticeably in the market before the off, that confirms connections have no strong expectation and the result can be read accordingly.

races.name: Racing Again Next Tuesday Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Shimmering Sands
runners_data.note: Back-to-back winner in cracking recent form, trainer Easterby yard in fair nick; handles Good ground well with nine course-and-distance-similar appearances confirming suitability, though tagged with a mild style-fit discount as a prominent type technically racing slightly out of natural lead role — in practice it is almost certain to lead here and that discount is minimal.

runners_data.name: Mwafaq
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey runner in superb current trim with wins at 7f-8f on Good ground; stepping up to 1m2f is the key question, but its prominent style gives it the best tactical position to exploit Shimmering Sands if the leader ties up, with apprentice claimer Ethan Tindall (5lb) keeping the weight competitive.

runners_data.name: Enamorus
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's 3-year-old is a hold-up type who has shown solid placed form without winning, and its recent outings have been at 7f-8f, making the 1m2f trip here a slight query; Cieren Fallon is a strong booking but the horse needs the pace to truly collapse for it to land a telling blow.

runners_data.name: Kitsune Power
runners_data.note: Genuinely won over this trip on Good ground last time out after a string of midfield finishes, and Tim Easterby's stable is firing — running only 6 days ago is worth noting for freshness; as a hold-up type it needs something to run at and a dawdling pace from Shimmering Sands is its biggest enemy today.

runners_data.name: Ziata
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's 3-year-old is a natural prominent racer whose best form has come on Soft ground, and having been pushed back to midfield on the pace map because Shimmering Sands holds the commanding position, it faces the dual challenge of racing out of role and a surface firmer than its optimum; 33 days off is also a mild query.

races.paceDynamic: Shimmering Sands is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Mwafaq and the redistributed Ziata as nominal prominent types, faces minimal credible pressure for the lead over Beverley's 1m2f trip on Good to Firm ground. Shimmering Sands can therefore dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from flag to flag, which at this trip on fast ground tends to reward the horse holding the rail and the rhythm rather than those tracking from behind. Mwafaq will push to sit prominently just off the pace, but Enamorus and Kitsune Power will need to make ground from further back, a task made harder if the leader controls the tempo. Note that the field holds more prominent-leaning types than can all occupy that position — Ziata, a genuine front-runner by profile, has been redistributed to midfield because Shimmering Sands is expected to dominate the early positions, meaning Ziata is likely to race further back than it would prefer. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-lead profiles, with Shimmering Sands ideally placed to control proceedings and Mwafaq best positioned to capitalise if the leader fades.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shimmering Sands Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Shimmering Sands leads without serious pressure and sets a measured pace that suits its recent front-running form.
scenarios.body: Shimmering Sands dictates throughout on the Good to Firm ground it handles well, winning back-to-back and showing its 7-year-old prime form at this trip; hold-up horses Enamorus and Kitsune Power find the steady tempo insufficient to generate the finish they need.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Mwafaq Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Mwafaq travels smoothly just off Shimmering Sands and produces a clean turn-of-foot in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Mwafaq, in excellent current form with three wins from its last five, stalks the leader and produces a decisive response inside the final two furlongs; its recent wins on Good ground make this trip and surface a strong fit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves strong enough to cut up the leaders and Enamorus or Kitsune Power close from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: Enamorus, ridden by Cieren Fallon, would need an unusually strong fractions to get into contention having shown form at up to 8f; Kitsune Power showed it can win at this trip on Good ground but its inconsistent recent form makes this a low-probability outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Ziata Recovers True Position
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses or runners become bunched and Ziata manages to reclaim a prominent berth from its redistributed midfield starting point.
scenarios.body: Ziata's true style is prominent but it is unlikely to secure that position against Shimmering Sands; if chaos erupts early and Ziata resets forward, its decent form over similar trips gives it a small chance, though its sole win came on Soft ground which tempers confidence on Good to Firm.

watchPoints.text: Shimmering Sands has won two on the bounce and faces next-to-no pressure for the lead — watch whether any runner attempts to challenge early, because if it is left completely alone the price of the favourite could compress further pre-race.

Mwafaq's stamina for 1m2f is unproven at pattern level — watch in-running for whether it is still travelling smoothly turning for home or being niggled along, which would sharply change how the closing stages play out.

Ziata's redistribution to midfield means it will be forced to race against its instincts — watch the early exchanges to see if jockey Jack Callan (3) attempts to push forward aggressively despite Shimmering Sands leading, which could cause interference or create an uneven pace.

Kitsune Power ran only six days ago — watch for any signs of staleness or a rider who settles it conservatively mid-race, as a fresh horse that was winning last time could outrun its odds if the fractions quicken late.
